title: Affordable Housing Levy payroll handling — general guidance
content: Employers handle Affordable Housing Levy deductions and remittance through KRA systems alongside payroll taxes. Correct payroll setup and timely filing avoid penalties. Keep levy declarations and payment records with monthly payroll.

title: Absconding and desertion allegations
content: Employers alleging desertion must still follow notice and hearing steps and compute dues. Employees delayed by emergency should communicate in writing. Keep messages and medical or incident proof.

title: Affordable Housing Levy on payslips
content: Check that the housing levy on the payslip matches official KRA computation and appears in remittance records. Raise mismatches with payroll in writing. Keep payslips and KRA statements.

title: Annual leave accrual and forfeiture
content: Employees accrue annual leave with pay and unused days have carry-over rules. Refused leave should be documented in writing. Keep leave applications, approvals, and balances on payslips.

title: Nursing breaks after maternity
content: Nursing mothers are entitled to reasonable breaks for breastfeeding on return to work. Agree scheduling in writing with the supervisor. Keep the agreement and any refusal notes.

title: Casual to term conversion rights
content: Casuals working continuously may qualify for conversion to term contracts with written particulars. Track days worked, pay, and supervisors. Raise conversion in writing before disputes arise.

title: Collective bargaining agreements
content: Registered CBAs set binding terms on pay and conditions for covered employees. Request a copy from the union or HR when disputing dues. Keep the CBA extract and payslips.

title: Certificate of service on exit
content: Every employee is entitled to a certificate of service stating the role and duration on termination. Request it in writing if withheld. Keep the certificate for future job applications.

title: Construction site workers: safety and pay
content: Site workers need protective gear, site induction, and documented pay for days worked. Report unsafe sites to DOSH with photos. Keep day-work records and payment messages.

title: Challenging hiring or promotion bias
content: Bias in hiring, pay, or promotion on protected grounds is prohibited. Keep adverts, shortlists, appraisals, and decision letters. Seek internal review, then labour office advice.

title: Rights of domestic workers
content: Domestic workers are employees entitled to contracts, minimum pay, rest, leave, and NSSF/SHIF remittance. Put terms in writing with off days and duties. Keep payment records and communications.

title: Filing a memorandum of claim at ELRC
content: ELRC claims attach the contract, termination letter, demand history, and computation of dues. File within limitation periods. Keep filed pleadings and service proof.

title: Computing terminal dues
content: Final dues combine notice pay, accrued leave, prorated salary, and contractual benefits less lawful deductions. Ask for an itemised statement. Keep payslips and the clearance form.

title: Fixed-term contracts and renewal expectations
content: Fixed-term contracts end on expiry, but repeated renewals can create expectations courts examine. Non-renewal notices should be in writing. Keep all successive contracts and renewal messages.

title: Work permits for foreign employees
content: Foreign workers need the correct permit class applied before reporting, with employer sponsorship. Verify validity rather than holding originals. Keep permit copies and receipts.

title: Reporting sexual harassment at work
content: Employers must have harassment policies and act on complaints. Report in writing to HR or management with dates, messages, and witnesses. Escalate to the labour office or ELRC if ignored.

title: Right to be heard before dismissal
content: Before termination for misconduct or poor performance, the employer must explain the reasons and hear the employee with a companion present. Minutes should be recorded. Keep the invitation, minutes, and outcome letter.

title: Househelp SHIF and NSSF registration
citation: Social Health Insurance Act, 2023; NSSF Act, 2013
content: Employers of domestic workers should register and remit SHIF and NSSF with monthly records. Confirm active cover for hospital visits. Keep registration and remittance receipts.

title: Reporting workplace injury the same day
content: Report injuries to the supervisor immediately, seek treatment, and ensure the employer files with DOSH. Keep treatment notes, incident reports, and witness names for compensation.

title: Interns and attachés: stipends and terms
content: Internships should have written terms on duration, stipend, supervision, and certificates. Unclear terms are clarified before reporting. Keep the offer letter, reports, and stipend records.

title: Jua kali artisan engagements
content: Fundis and workshop hands should agree scope, price, timelines, and materials in writing. Payment disputes rely on messages and delivery proof. Keep quotations and M-Pesa records.

title: Filing at the county labour office
content: Complaints are lodged with contracts, payslips, and a dated statement. Officers attempt conciliation before referral. Keep the complaint number and conciliation notes.

title: Maternity leave and protection
content: Female employees qualify for maternity leave with pay subject to service conditions, and dismissal on pregnancy grounds is prohibited. Notify in writing with expected dates. Keep antenatal records and the leave approval.

title: Dismissal during pregnancy or leave
content: Termination connected to pregnancy or maternity leave is prohibited and actionable. Keep antenatal records, leave approvals, and the dismissal letter for the labour office or ELRC.

title: Minimum wage orders by area and sector
content: Minimum wages vary by urban area and occupation under gazetted orders reviewed periodically. Confirm the current order for the county and job group. Keep payslips and the applicable order printout.

title: Non-compete and confidentiality clauses
citation: Law of Contract Act; Employment Act
content: Restraint clauses must be reasonable in scope and duration to be enforceable. Get advice before signing or breaching. Keep the signed contract and any breach allegations.

title: Notice periods under the Employment Act
content: Notice length follows the contract or the statutory scale based on pay intervals where the contract is silent. Payment in lieu is allowed. Keep the contract, payslips, and termination notice to compute dues.

title: Checking NSSF remittance as an employee
content: Employees can verify NSSF contributions through statements and the fund channels. Report missing remittances first to the employer, then the fund. Keep payslips and fund statements.

title: Overtime pay and working hours
citation: Employment Act, 2007; Regulation of Wages Orders
content: Normal hours and overtime rates follow the Act and wage orders for the sector. Keep rosters, clock records, and payslips showing hours. Claim arrears first in writing to the employer.

title: Paternity leave for fathers
content: Male employees are entitled to paternity leave with pay on the birth of a child. Apply in writing with the expected date and birth notification. Keep the approval and birth records.

title: P9 forms and tax on exit
content: Employers issue P9 forms summarising annual pay and tax for returns and new-employer onboarding. Request the P9 and final payslip on exit. Keep KRA returns and iTax records.

title: Itemised payslips every pay day
content: Employees are entitled to written pay statements showing gross, deductions, and net. Missing payslips weaken loan and dispute claims. Request them monthly and archive copies.

title: Performance improvement plans
content: PIPs should set measurable targets, support, and review dates. Challenge vague or shifting goals in writing. Keep appraisals, targets, and review minutes.

title: Probation periods and confirmation
content: Probation must be agreed in writing with a limited duration and possible extension. Unsatisfactory probation still requires notice and a hearing. Keep the probation clause, appraisals, and confirmation letter.

title: Redundancy notice and severance
content: Redundancies require advance notice to the employee, union, and labour office plus severance computation. Selection criteria must be fair. Keep the redundancy notice, selection records, and payment schedule.

title: Resigning properly and notice
content: Resign in writing with the contractual notice and handover. The employer must settle dues and issue a certificate of service. Keep the resignation acceptance and clearance records.

title: Retirement age and pension processing
content: Retirement follows the contract or scheme rules with notice and benefits processing. Start pension paperwork early with IDs and service records. Keep benefit statements and correspondence.

title: Delivery rider and driver engagements
content: Rider terms should state pay model, fuel, maintenance, and accident cover. Classify correctly as employee or contractor from the facts. Keep trip records and payment statements.

title: Workplace safety committees
content: Larger workplaces must have safety committees and risk assessments. Workers can raise hazards in writing to the committee and DOSH. Keep complaint copies and inspection notes.

title: Delayed salaries: steps to take
content: Demand arrears in writing with months owed and amounts, then escalate to the labour office with payslips and bank statements. Keep the demand letter and delivery proof.

title: Secondment and transfer of employees
content: Secondments should be documented with the host, duration, reporting, and who pays. Refusals of transfer depend on contract mobility clauses. Keep the secondment letter and pay records.

title: Private security guards: hours and pay
citation: Employment Act; Private Security Regulation Act, 2016
content: Guards face long shifts that must still respect hours, overtime, and rest rules, with licensed employers. Keep duty rosters, payslips, and licence details when raising underpayment.

title: Service pay on termination
content: Employees without pension or gratuity coverage may qualify for service pay for completed years. Compute from the contract and payslips. Keep NSSF statements and gratuity records to prove eligibility.

title: Checking SHIF remittance as an employee
content: Employees should confirm SHIF registration and monthly remittance to keep cover active for dependants. Raise gaps with HR, then the fund. Keep registration details and remittance confirmations.

title: Sick leave procedure and certificates
content: Sick leave follows notification and medical certificates for longer absence, with full and half-pay phases. Submit certificates promptly. Keep medical notes and delivery proof.

title: Protected strikes and lock-outs
content: Strikes in essential services and without statutory notice lose protection. Unions must follow dispute and ballot steps. Keep strike notices and conciliator correspondence.

title: Summary dismissal for gross misconduct
content: Summary dismissal without notice is allowed only for gross misconduct such as theft, violence, or wilful neglect, and the employer must still hear the employee. Demand written reasons and keep the dismissal letter for challenge.

title: Board of management teachers contracts
content: BOM teachers should hold written contracts stating pay, subjects, and term. Unpaid arrears are claimed first in writing to the board. Keep contracts, timetables, and payment records.

title: Transfer to another branch or town
content: Transfers depend on mobility clauses and must be communicated with timelines and allowances. Object in writing where hardship or contract breach arises. Keep the transfer letter and contract.

title: Challenging unfair termination
content: Dismissals without valid reason or fair procedure can be challenged at the labour office and the ELRC for reinstatement or compensation. Act within limitation periods. Keep the dismissal letter, contract, and payslips.

title: Joining a trade union
content: Employees may join registered unions of their choice with check-off deductions on written authority. Victimisation for union activity is prohibited. Keep membership cards and deduction records.

title: Volunteers and stipend disputes
content: Volunteer terms should be written with hours, stipend, and duration to avoid later employment claims. Disputes turn on control and pay evidence. Keep the volunteer agreement and records.

title: Answering show-cause and warning letters
content: Respond to show-cause letters factually within the deadline, attaching supporting evidence and witnesses. Keep copies of the letter, response, and delivery proof for the hearing.

title: Work injury compensation claims
content: Compensation covers medical costs and assessed disability following reported workplace injuries. File with medical reports and employer records. Keep DOSH reports and payment decisions.

title: Employment Act, 2007
content: The Employment Act governs terms of employment including contracts, wages, working hours, leave, termination, and remedies. Employers must give written particulars of employment and follow fair procedure before termination. Keep contracts, payslips, warning letters, and termination notices.

title: Employment contracts and casual work — general guidance
content: Employees should have written terms covering job, pay, hours, and leave. Casual workers engaged continuously may qualify for conversion protections. Keep offer letters, timesheets, M-Pesa salary records, and any messages about duties or pay.

title: Workplace discrimination and harassment — general guidance
content: Discrimination and sexual harassment at work are prohibited. Employers should have reporting policies. Keep messages, witness names, incident dates, and copies of complaints made to HR or management for labour office or court referral.

title: Leave entitlements — general guidance
content: Employees accrue rights to annual leave, sick leave, maternity and paternity leave subject to qualifying conditions. Denial of leave or dismissal for pregnancy-related reasons may be challenged. Keep leave applications, approvals, medical notes, and birth records.

title: Payslips and lawful deductions — general guidance
content: Employees in Kenya are entitled to clear payslips showing gross pay, statutory deductions, and other lawful deductions such as approved loans or contributions. Employers should not deduct wages except as allowed by law or written agreement. Keep payslips, contracts, and deduction authorisations.

title: Redundancy — general guidance
content: Redundancy must follow due process including consultation and notice to the labour office and union where applicable. Affected employees may be entitled to severance pay. Keep redundancy notices, selection criteria, and payment records.

title: Workplace safety and injury — general guidance
citation: Occupational Safety and Health Act, No. 15 of 2007; Work Injury Benefits Act, 2007
content: Employers must provide a safe workplace and report serious accidents. Injured employees should seek treatment, report the injury to the employer promptly, and keep medical and DOSH reports for compensation claims under the Work Injury Benefits Act.

title: Terminal dues and clearance on exit — general guidance
content: Employees leaving work in Kenya are generally entitled to settlement of earned wages, accrued leave, notice pay where applicable, and any contractual benefits. Employers commonly use a clearance process for tools, advances, and handover before final payment. Keep payslips, clearance forms, and final payment records.

title: Termination and unfair dismissal — general guidance
content: Employers must give notice or pay in lieu of notice except for gross misconduct, and must follow fair hearing procedure. Unfair or wrongful dismissal can be challenged through the labour office or the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Act quickly and keep the dismissal letter and final dues computation.

title: Wages, overtime and deductions — general guidance
content: Employees are entitled to timely payment of wages, regulated working hours, and regulated deductions. Minimum wages vary by area and sector under wage orders. Keep payslips, bank or M-Pesa statements, and records of hours worked and deductions.

title: Hiring staff and written particulars — general guidance
content: Employees engaged for more than a short period should receive written particulars of wages, hours, leave and termination terms. Employers must keep employment records and statutory returns. Keep signed contracts and payroll records for inspections and disputes.

title: Labour disputes — general guidance
content: Employees with disputes should document incidents, seek internal resolution, and may contact the county labour office or legal aid for unfair dismissal, wage, or safety issues. Serious disputes go to the Employment and Labour Relations Court. Keep a dated timeline of events.

title: NSSF contributions for staff — general guidance
content: Employers must register with NSSF, deduct employee contributions where applicable and remit employer and employee contributions by the due date. Late remittance attracts penalties and interest under the Act. Keep NSSF returns and payment receipts with payroll.

title: NSSF and SHIF deductions — general guidance
citation: NSSF Act, 2013; Social Health Insurance Act, 2023
content: Employers must remit statutory deductions including NSSF and the Social Health Insurance Fund where applicable, and employees should receive payslips showing deductions. Check remittance statements and raise missing remittances with the employer, then the fund or legal aid.

title: PAYE for employers — general guidance
citation: Income Tax Act, Cap. 470; Tax Procedures Act, 2015
content: Employers who pay emoluments must register as employers with KRA, deduct PAYE and remit it by the due date with monthly returns. Annual employer reconciliations and P9 forms support employees' tax filings. Keep payroll, remittance receipts and P9 copies.

title: Salary advances and staff loans — general guidance
content: Salary advances and staff loans should be in writing stating amount, repayment instalments and how balances are treated on exit. Statutory limits on deductions from wages protect minimum take-home pay. Keep signed advance forms and payroll deduction records.

title: SHIF contributions for staff — general guidance
content: Employers and employees participate in the Social Health Insurance Fund under the current SHIF framework, with contributions remitted through the designated system. Registration and timely remittance keep staff cover active. Keep registration details and monthly remittance confirmations.
